declarations.rationale: Determinism smoke for the identity gate. It rejects against the complete measured dataset, so its recorded zero-accepted result is a statement about GLOBAL discovery headroom on a near-complete factorial matrix -- not a statement about how much a low-data learner could generate. Retained under its executed protocol.
Role-change contract smoke under the same global rule; its null-eligibility finding is a global-novelty statement.
Candidate-ranking smoke under the same global rule; its zero-accepted result is a global-novelty statement.
AE refit; resolves the same rule the AE search froze.
Joint AE + transfer search on the same low-data protocol.
Defines the taxonomy and the typed policy; performs no generation.
Builds one chemical control from whichever rule its caller declares, and records the resolved mode in the control's frozen config.
Recombination generator. The resolved policy also bounds the generation budget, so the scope decides pool size as well as acceptance.
Anonymous generator. Resolves the caller's policy and folds in the labeled training frame's own identities; the scientific choice belongs to the caller.
Wraps the recombination generator and forwards its caller's rule.
External-family typed transfer. Rejects against whatever key set the adapter caller supplies; defaults to the training frame's identities.
A latent coordinate has no seven-role reaction identity. Chemical duplicate questions are recorded as null, not false: they are not answerable, which is a different statement from 'answered no'.

Reaction-component reordering within a role. Identity-preserving only while the caller passes same-role columns; the module documents that it does not infer chemical exchangeability and refuses an empty column list rather than guessing.
Typed generator; same conduit contract as the anonymous generator.
Pool builder. Accepts either an explicit policy or the historical global key contract, and binds the resolved mode into the pool hash.
Dispatcher; propagates the callee's semantics unchanged.

Duplication and reweighting controls reuse measured chemistry by design; the feature-space controls (nearest-neighbour pseudo-labelling, self-training, feature mixup) create coordinates with no seven-role identity and record chemical_identity_applicable=False.

RDKit atom renumbering produces a different SMILES string for the same molecule and copies the measured label. Canonicalization is an involution over this transform, so an identity gate would reject 100% of the output by definition. The gate must not apply.
The shared identity gate. It applies whichever CandidateScopePolicy it is handed and has no eligibility opinion of its own.
Generated feature coordinates carry no asserted chemical identity; feature-hash deduplication is applied, chemical-identity rejection is not.
Phase 11 matched-budget controls. Asks whether chemical augmentation helps a low-data learner, so it defaults to observed-only and the post-hoc validator applies the same declared rule.
Development reanalysis. Runs both modes side by side and freezes each pool before the withheld-cell oracle reads any hidden yield.
Matched corrected anonymous/typed transfer at low data fractions.
Defines the four partitions and builds typed policies from them. Has no field that can carry hidden outer-training identities into generation.
Reads hidden outer-training yields only after candidates and pseudo-labels are frozen and hash-verified. Performs no generation.
Refit and single outer-test batch. Must resolve the same rule the search froze, or the refit pool would differ from the selected one.

Phase 12 pseudo-label accuracy and interval calibration. Its withheld cells are a condition group carved out of the labeled training subset rather than the hidden outer-training partition, so it measures a proxy population; the withheld-cell oracle covers the population this audit is about.

Frozen-policy search. Reads candidate_scope.mode and binds it into the scientific config hash, so the declared rule is part of the frozen policy identity. Defaults to the historical prospective rule so a pre-audit config reproduces exactly.
Phase 18 prospective discovery. A proposed reaction must never have been measured anywhere in the complete historical dataset, so global membership is the correct and intended eligibility rule.
Recommendation simulation ranks reactions for prospective execution; a recommendation that is already measured is not a recommendation.

Phase 14/15. Already correct before this audit: its key set is the phase's own visible rows (inner policy-fit rows during search, saved training rows during placement and final), never the complete dataset, and a hash guard hard-fails if a pool consumes anything else. The `global_measured_identity_keys` parameter name is historical; the value passed is observed-only.
Compares feature encodings with no augmentation at all.
Legacy anonymous transfer runner on a low-data protocol.
Supervised-AE runner whose training pool depends on transferred candidates.

External reaction-family adapter. Low-data augmentation benefit on a second family; eligibility follows the labeled training partition. The empirical datasets remain blocked, so only the semantics change.
Legacy typed transfer runner on a low-data protocol.
